title: Physics-guided machine learning for sim-to-real calibration of NV diamond magnetometers
authors: Jonathan Daniel, Martin Y. Kim, Jesse Hernandez, Emanuel Suarez, Sangwoo Lee, Jinhee Lee, Je-Hyung Kim
abstract: Ensemble nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond enable robust vector magnetometry in unshielded environments, yet deployment remains bottlenecked by complex calibration and a reliance on external data references. Conventional statistical machine learning requires an exorbitantly large volume of training data and suffers from severe simulation-to-reality mismatches. To address this, we introduce a physics-guided hybrid machine learning framework that embeds the Zeeman splitting directly into the learning pipeline. Our physics-guided model significantly reduces the average tracking error demonstrating a 372-fold precision improvement over purely statistical baselines. Furthermore, our hybrid architecture pairs a sparse physical measurement with scalable synthetic data generation, seamlessly incorporating real-world hardware non-idealities. When deployed to decode uncalibrated, raw experimental ODMR data, our framework delivers exceptional predictive accuracy for the scalar magnetic field. This work paves the way toward self-calibrated sensors while establishing a machine learning training method applicable to other data-scarce physical systems
summary: The paper presents a novel physics-guided hybrid machine learning framework to solve the calibration challenge in NV diamond magnetometers. By embedding known physical laws, the model overcomes the limitations of purely data-driven approaches, achieving dramatic improvements in magnetic field measurement precision. This methodology establishes a general paradigm for building self-calibrating AI tools for other data-scarce physical systems.
main_problem: Deploying NV diamond magnetometers in unshielded environments requires self-calibration, which is bottlenecked by data scarcity and the simulation-to-reality mismatch.
main_result: The physics-guided hybrid ML framework achieved a 372-fold precision improvement over purely statistical baselines, enabling exceptional predictive accuracy on raw experimental data.
method: The authors developed a hybrid machine learning framework that embeds the deterministic Zeeman splitting relationship directly into the neural network architecture, combining sparse physical measurements with scalable synthetic data generation.
model_or_system: The system utilizes ensemble Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond for vector magnetometry, governed by a spin Hamiltonian. Measurements are performed via Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (ODMR) spectroscopy.
key_observables: ODMR spectrum (fluorescence intensity dip), scalar magnetic field vector (B).

main_assumptions: The method assumes that physical laws (like the Zeeman splitting) can be deterministically embedded as constraints into the ML training pipeline to overcome data limitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the NV center setup, the hybrid pipeline architecture, and performance comparisons showing the massive error reduction achieved by the physics-guided model over purely stochastic baselines, including validation on raw experimental spectra.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical problem (NV magnetometry calibration), details the limitations of conventional ML, proposes the physics-guided hybrid ML framework, validates it first on synthetic data, and finally demonstrates its success on raw, uncalibrated experimental data.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete methodology for integrating fundamental physical constraints (like Hamiltonian terms) into data-driven models, which is highly relevant for developing robust quantum sensing and characterization tools.

The dataset undergoes a K-fold cross- validation branching into stochastic and physics-guided model. The outputs of the two models are fed into another layer of stochastic model forming an ensemble neural network, yielding the final outputs.
